title: Nerve Data Gateway User Configuration (v1.1)
description: Schema for the Data Gateway `config.json` file with `version` = "1.1". Introduced in Data Gateway 1.1.0. Adds the `sql-client` endpoint type and the `sql-columnar-writer` / `sql-binary-writer` output types on top of v1.0. Authoritative source: data-gateway-documentation/configuration/config-schema-v1.1.json.

$schema.description: Optional URL of this schema — allows editors to provide autocompletion and validation.

version.description: Configuration file schema version. Must be the literal string "1.1" for this schema.

endpoints.description: Every external system the Data Gateway connects to (data sources and sinks).

connections.description: Wires exactly one input on one endpoint to exactly one output on another endpoint.

PasswordPolicy.description: Global characteristics of ALL passwords the Data Gateway generates. Optional; every field has a secure default, so omitting the object (or any field) keeps existing configs valid.

minLength.description: Minimum generated length. The generator picks a random length in [minLength, maxLength].

maxLength.description: Maximum generated length. Must be >= minLength.

symbols.description: Symbol alphabet used when useSymbols is true. Must be a (non-empty) subset of the fixed set !#$%*+-.:=?@^_~ — no other symbols are permitted. This set deliberately excludes quote/backslash/space to keep exported creds safe in SQL literals, connection strings and .env files.

id.description: Identifier — must be unique among all endpoints.

endpointType.description: Type of the endpoint. Determines which additional parameters are valid.

url.description: MQTT broker URL. `mqtt://` requires `security.tlsEnabled = false`; `mqtts://` requires `security.tlsEnabled = true`.

reconnectInterval.description: Seconds to wait before each reconnection attempt after unexpected connection loss.

version.description: MQTT protocol version to use for the connection.

clientID.description: MQTT client identifier used when connecting to the broker.

websockets.description: If true, use MQTT over WebSockets.

reconnectInterval.description: Seconds to wait before each reconnection attempt after unexpected connection loss.

outputs.description: The opcua-client endpoint currently does not support outputs — must be an empty array.

dbType.description: Database system to connect to. Determines the write protocol used and the valid output types.

host.description: Hostname or IP address of the database server.

port.description: PostgreSQL wire protocol port. Default 5432 for `postgresql` and `timescaledb`; default 8812 for `questdb` (used only for management operations such as CREATE TABLE).

ilpPort.description: QuestDB only: HTTP ILP (InfluxDB Line Protocol) port used for data ingestion. Ignored for postgresql and timescaledb.

database.description: Name of the target database. Not applicable for questdb (single-database system).

reconnectInterval.description: Seconds to wait before each reconnection attempt after unexpected connection loss.

bootstrap.description: Optional self-provisioning of a least-privilege gateway DB role against a vanilla PostgreSQL/TimescaleDB. Not supported for dbType=questdb (rejected by the supervisor validator).

admin.description: One-time bootstrap seed: an existing admin/superuser account used only for the first provisioning. Expected to stop working after rotation.

gatewayRoleName.description: Name of the least-privilege login role the gateway creates/maintains and uses for writing.

rotateAdminPassword.description: After a successful bootstrap using the public seed, rotate the admin password to a strong random value (break-glass recovery path).

exportPublicKey.description: age X25519 recipient; encrypts ALL exported credential files (rotated admin always, human user if created). REQUIRED when bootstrap is enabled unless allowPlaintextExport is true.

allowPlaintextExport.description: INSECURE opt-out: when true, exported credential files are written in plaintext and exportPublicKey may be omitted. Not recommended.

exportUser.description: Optional human login role to create alongside the gateway role.

regenerate.description: opaque nonce; change its value to force generation of a fresh human credential on next apply.

inputs.description: The sql-client endpoint does not support inputs — must be an empty array.

UserPasswordLogin.description: Credentials for username / password authentication. Omit the whole object for anonymous.

MqttSecurity.description: TLS / SSL settings for the MQTT endpoint.

ca.description: Filename of the CA certificate (PEM) used to verify the broker certificate.

keyPassword.description: Password for the client key file.

tlsInsecure.description: If true, the broker certificate is not verified.

ca.description: Filename of the CA certificate (PEM) used to verify the server certificate.

keyPassword.description: Password for the client key file.

SqlSecurity.description: TLS settings for the SQL endpoint.

ca.description: Filename of the CA certificate (PEM) used to verify the server certificate.

tlsInsecure.description: If true, the server certificate is not verified.

willTopic.description: Topic for the last will testament (LWT) message.

SqlAdvanced.description: Write performance tuning for SQL endpoints.

batchSize.description: Number of rows to accumulate before a write is issued. Values >1 improve throughput, especially with QuestDB ILP.

flushIntervalMS.description: Maximum time (ms) between flushes. Ensures data is written even if a full batchSize batch has not accumulated. Has no effect when batchSize is 1.

id.description: Identifier — must be unique among all inputs of the endpoint.

messageFormat.description: Format of the incoming MQTT message payload.

variableSchema.description: Optional. Declares expected types for variables in JSON-format messages. Ignored for binary and protobuf inputs. If a declared variable's arriving JSON value does not match the declared type, that variable is dropped with a warning. Undeclared variables have their type inferred.

VariableSchemaNode.description: Either a leaf type string or a nested object mapping child variable names to VariableSchemaNodes.

oneOf.description: Scalar or array type for a single variable.
Nested variable group — maps child names to their types.

topic.description: Topic to subscribe to. Supports MQTT wildcards `+` and `#`.

rateLimit.description: 0 = no rate limit. >0 = maximum number of messages received per second (sliding window); additional messages are dropped.

id.description: Identifier — must be unique among all outputs of the endpoint.

messageFormat.description: Format of the outgoing MQTT message payload.

timestampFormat.description: Format of the `timestamp` field when `messageFormat` is `json`. `unix-ns` (default) emits a 64-bit integer (nanoseconds since Unix epoch). `rfc3339nano` emits an RFC 3339 string with nanosecond resolution in UTC (e.g. "2023-11-14T22:13:20.123456789Z"). Ignored when `messageFormat` is `protobuf`.

id.description: Identifier — must be unique among all inputs of the endpoint.

pollingIntervalMS.description: Polling interval in milliseconds. Only for inputType = opcua-polling.

samplingIntervalMS.description: Interval at which the server should sample the object (ms). Only for inputType = opcua-subscriber.

publishingIntervalMS.description: Interval at which the server should publish the object (ms). Only for inputType = opcua-subscriber.

node.description: OPC UA node id of the object to be polled / subscribed.

nameFromNodeID.description: If true, the resulting variable name is the full OPC UA node id; otherwise the display name of the OPC UA object is used.

register.description: If true, register the node (or all sub-nodes for a folder) at the OPC UA server. See https://reference.opcfoundation.org/Core/Part4/v104/docs/5.8.5

id.description: Identifier — must be unique among all outputs of the endpoint.

table.description: Name of the target table. Must exist unless autoCreateTable is true.

timestampColumn.description: Name of the column that receives the message timestamp. Designated timestamp for QuestDB; hypertable time dimension for TimescaleDB.

excludeVariables.description: Regex patterns (anchored / full-match). Any variable whose name matches at least one pattern is excluded from writing.

autoCreateTable.description: If true, create the table if it does not exist and add new columns as new variable names appear. If false, unknown variables are dropped with a warning.

retentionPeriod.description: Retention period in minutes. When greater than 0, rows older than this value are periodically deleted from the target table. 0 disables retention.

nestedVariableDelimiter.description: Character used to join path segments when a nested variable is flattened into a column name (e.g. "motor_temperature"). Not expressible here: "." is rejected at runtime when the endpoint's dbType is "questdb" (same style of runtime-only restriction as the sql-binary-writer + questdb incompatibility).

table.description: Name of the target table. Must exist unless autoCreateTable is true.

timestampColumn.description: Name of the timestamp column. Set to the current time at the moment of writing.

dataColumn.description: Name of the column that stores the binary payload (BYTEA in PostgreSQL / TimescaleDB).

autoCreateTable.description: If true, the table is created automatically (with timestampColumn and dataColumn) if it does not exist.

retentionPeriod.description: Retention period in minutes. When greater than 0, rows older than this value are periodically deleted from the target table. 0 disables retention.

id.description: Identifier — must be unique among connections.

endpoint.description: Id of the endpoint that holds the input to connect.

input.description: Id of the input to connect.

endpoint.description: Id of the endpoint that holds the output to connect.

output.description: Id of the output to connect.
